candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide evidence-based education and referrals that reduce chronic disease risk and support healthy lifestyle behaviors
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — structured lifestyle intervention for prediabetes
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with prediabetes that evidence-based diabetes prevention programs use structured lifestyle coaching, modest weight loss, healthier eating, and regular physical activity to reduce progression to type 2 diabetes.

options.A: The program uses structured coaching to support healthier eating, about 5% to 7% weight loss, and increased physical activity, including a goal of at least 150 minutes per week.
options.B: The program focuses primarily on starting glucose-lowering medication rather than lifestyle behavior change.
options.C: The main strategy is eliminating nearly all carbohydrate-containing foods for one year.
options.D: The program is intended mainly for people who already have diagnosed type 2 diabetes and need medication management.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC’s National Diabetes Prevention Program is a yearlong structured lifestyle-change program for adults with prediabetes or high risk for type 2 diabetes. The CDC PreventT2 curriculum promotes modest weight loss of about 5% to 7% and increased physical activity; the research underlying the program used a goal of at least 150 minutes of activity per week and substantially reduced progression to type 2 diabetes. B and C misrepresent the intervention. D is incorrect because the National DPP lifestyle-change program is designed to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes rather than manage established type 2 diabetes.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC-recognized diabetes prevention lifestyle programs are structured, yearlong interventions emphasizing modest 5%–7% weight loss, healthier eating, and increased physical activity, with the foundational DPP using a ≥150-minutes-per-week activity goal to reduce progression to type 2 diabetes.
candidate.source_document_title: What Is the National DPP?; PreventT2 Curriculum and Handouts; Preventing Type 2 Diabetes with the Lifestyle Change Program
candidate.source_locator: ‘What Is the National DPP?’ — original DPP lifestyle intervention used calorie reduction, ≥150 minutes/week physical activity, and achieved 5%–7% weight loss with 58% risk reduction; ‘PreventT2 Curriculum and Handouts’ — promotes modest 5%–7% weight loss and increased physical activity through a 12-month program; Lifestyle Change Program — designed for people with prediabetes or at risk, not those already diagnosed with type 2 diabetes
